articleTitle: An introduction to the Iridium(R) system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Opportunities Offered by Advanced Satellite Systems - Day 1 (Ref. No. 1998/484)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the Iridium(R) system. The Iridium system is owned and operated by Iridium LLC, and forms the technological 'backbone' of the world's first worldwide telephone company. The paper details the background and history of the system's development phase. The technology that has been developed is then discussed, along with an overview of the telephony services offered to the user.

articleTitle: The ICO system for personal communications by satellite
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Opportunities Offered by Advanced Satellite Systems - Day 1 (Ref. No. 1998/484)
abstract: The ICO is a satellite-based mobile communications system designed primarily to provide services to handheld phones. The system will offer digital voice, data, facsimile, and a suite of messaging services anywhere in the intended environments world-wide. The system design integrates mobile satellite communications capability with terrestrial networks and employs, among others, handheld mobile telephones which offer services similar to normal cellular phones, in outdoor environments. It will route calls from terrestrial networks through ground stations (called satellite access nodes or "SANs") which will select a satellite through which the call will be connected. Calls from a mobile terminal will be routed via the satellite constellation to the appropriate fixed or mobile networks or to another mobile satellite terminal. Handsets will be produced by major manufacturers of telecommunications equipment, benefiting from terrestrial cellular/PCS technology. Single-mode satellite-only versions will be available, but most are expected to be capable of dual-mode operation with both satellite and terrestrial cellular/PCS systems.

articleTitle: Introduction to Globalstar/sup TM/ [satellite communication system]
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Opportunities Offered by Advanced Satellite Systems - Day 1 (Ref. No. 1998/484)
abstract: A new communications tool-the hand-held satellite telephone-will be available to business people before the turn of the century. At about the same time, affordable, basic telephony-through fixed-site satellite telephones-will be available for the first time to millions of citizens of developing economies. Globalstar will usher in both. Globalstar is a low-Earth-orbiting (LEO) satellite-based digital telecommunications system that will offer wireless telephone and other telecommunications services worldwide beginning in 1999. Globalstar will provide low-cost, high quality telephony and other digital telecommunications services such as data transmission, paging, facsimile and position location to areas currently under served or not served by existing wireline and cellular telecommunications systems.

articleTitle: Technology for the future marketplace: a perspective on Ka and on-board processing technology
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Opportunities Offered by Advanced Satellite Systems - Day 1 (Ref. No. 1998/484)
abstract: Modular product line satellites are now the norm for high-power transponder satellite markets. Advances in multi-beam Ka components and on-board processing have been stimulated by NASA studies and MILSATCOM developments, These advanced payload technologies are still, however, in development. The challenge then is to coordinate the simultaneous evolution of advanced payload technology development and advanced high-power modular product line satellites. This paper explores the state of advanced payload technologies and postulates product line partitions that may lend themselves to modular cost-effective integration of advanced payload technologies into the next generation satellites. Modular cost-effective integration and suppliers will be necessary if the cost of mature advanced multi-beam Ka-band and on-board processing satellites is to approach the commodity pricing environment driving current high-power transponder satellites. These partitions may also indicate a focus for the multiple worldwide study and development activities.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Opportunities Offered by Advanced Satellite Systems - Day 1 (Ref. No. 1998/484)
abstract: The Horizons programme is Inmarsat's fourth generation system, designed to provide multimedia services to mobile users, worldwide. Horizons will develop a new generation of user terminals which will interface to standard portable computer (PC) devices, including laptop and palmtops to provide users with the capability to access the full range of multimedia services in remote areas where a terrestrial infrastructure is not available. Inmarsat plans to implement a new constellation of satellites and an optimised ground segment architecture to enable the Horizons system to provide these services, worldwide. This paper describes the key aspects of the Horizons programme, including the space segment, the ground segment, and also the user terminals.

articleTitle: Trends in communications satellite platform design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Opportunities Offered by Advanced Satellite Systems - Day 1 (Ref. No. 1998/484)
abstract: For more than twenty years, communications satellite manufacturers, launch vehicle providers, and satellite operators have participated in the gradual evolution of the satellite communications business. Deregulation, changing business climates, and major changes in the telecommunications market are contributing to dramatic shifts in the perception of satellites as part of an integrated communications strategy. The latest generation of satellite platforms introduces capabilities to support new kinds of services, and to radically change the way satellites are manufactured.
